<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Conversation ingest is pull-only and nothing schedules it: the daemon has no conversation poller (convo_ingest.rs:249 assumes harness hooks that were never installed), so every transcript is indexed as of the last time a human typed `conversation ingest` and rots from that second — measured: unicorn's session 22 turns vs 984 lines over three days; grim-gurgeh's omp session 110 turns vs a 13 MB file; fleet-wide 106 live session files in 7 days against 109 conversations indexed ever. Separately the git-ai metrics-db route opens a file that does not exist (~/.git-ai/metrics.sqlite3 vs ~/.git-ai/internal/metrics-db), so copilot ingest has never worked, and `verify` tells a caller holding a not-yet-persisted session id to 'run ingest'. This packet adds a fifth Reconcile implementor — a daemon-side poller over the NATIVE session stores (claude, omp) keyed on FILES, never on pij seat rows — that enqueues the existing idempotent ingest when a session file has bytes beyond its durable cursor; makes the rot visible in `status` and `doctor`; distinguishes 'no session file yet' from 'not indexed'; and fixes the metrics-db path. The readers already exist and work; this ships the loop that runs them.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- a daemon reconciler (`convo_poll`, fifth `Reconcile` implementor, tick-counted like retention) that every poll cadence enumerates `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl` (+ `<uuid>/subagents/*.jsonl`) and `~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slug>/<ts>_<uuid>.jsonl`, and for every session file whose on-disk size exceeds its durable ingest cursor (or that has no cursor and was modified within the lookback window) calls `convo_ingest::submit_after` with the file-derived (harness, session_id, folder) — identity comes from the FILE, never from a pij seat row
- the poller is a no-op on an unchanged store (size == cursor enqueues nothing — proven by test) and bounded on a cold start (a per-pass submission cap with a stagger via `submit_after`, so 100+ backlog sessions do not land as one burst)
- `status` gains an additive `conversations` block: last_poll_at, per-harness sessions tracked / behind (size > cursor) / newest_ingest_at; `doctor` gains a `conversations` row that says in one line whether ingest is flowing, stalled, or disabled, and whether the git-ai store exists — so 'quiet because nothing changed' and 'quiet because dead' stop looking identical (DL-001)
- `verify`/`ingest` distinguish 'no session file exists for this id yet' (new catalog code, fix text: the harness has not persisted it; the poller picks it up when written) from 'not indexed' (existing code) — the pij `harness_session` lazy-persist case named in evidence.md §4
- the git-ai metrics-db source resolves its path by probing `~/.git-ai/internal/metrics-db` then `~/.git-ai/metrics.sqlite3`; the ingest ROUTE fails fast with an honest message when neither opens instead of accepting and failing in the job; the doctor row reports the resolved path or its absence
- two config knobs under `[indexing]`: `conversation_poll_ticks` (shared 5s ticks between polls; default 12 = one minute; 0 disables) and `conversation_lookback_days` (default 14; files older than this with no cursor are ignored); both documented in the config template; deny_unknown_fields respected
- real usage on prod after o-prime's bounce: grim-gurgeh's omp session (13 MB, indexed at 110 turns) advances past 110 without anyone typing ingest, within two poll cadences; a fresh claude session started in a new directory is indexed within two cadences; `status` and `doctor` show the block/row; the second poll after catch-up enqueues nothing (log shows `reconciled` quiet)

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- polling the pij ledger (seat-keyed, not file-keyed) or the git-ai metrics-db for copilot sessions — v1 fixes the metrics-db PATH only; copilot polling is a follow-up once the path fix is proven
- changing the readers, the ordinal/grouping rules (FROZEN — see claude.rs:60-75 and metrics_db.rs), the cursor ledger semantics, or the conversation guid derivation
- a hook-based trigger (harness fs3-convo ingest from a Stop hook) — may coexist later; the enqueue is idempotent, so it is additive and out of scope here
- any change to search, summarisation cost policy, or the runner's job claim loop (a reconciler ENQUEUES, it never runs the job — reconcile.rs scope guard)
